chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and the messenger of his uncle, Abdullah ibn Ali, came and said to him, 'Your uncle says to you: We sought the 'Aqiqah (sacrificial animal for a newborn) but could not find it, so what do you think if we give its price in charity?' He said, 'No, indeed Allah the Exalted loves the feeding (of the poor) and the shedding of blood (i.e., the actual slaughter of the animal).'

key_terms.إِرَاقَة الدِّمَاء: Iraqat al-Dima': The shedding of blood, referring specifically to the ritual slaughter
key_terms.الْإِطْعَام: Al-It'am: Feeding (the poor), referring to the act of providing food
key_terms.الْعَقِيقَة: Aqiqah: The sacrificial animal slaughtered upon the birth of a child

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred method for performing Aqiqah if an animal cannot be found?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the ritual slaughter (*dhabh*) is an essential component of the 'Aqiqah, distinguishing it from general charity (*sadaqah*). The Imam emphasizes that Allah loves the physical act of slaughtering and shedding blood, thereby establishing the preference for the actual sacrifice over its monetary equivalent in this specific context. This ruling underscores the importance of replicating the Prophet's practice (*Sunnah*) in its entirety rather than merely fulfilling the financial obligation.
